sources.full_text:
Exercise increased caution in Tajikistan due to the risk of terrorism , unexploded landmines , and limited ability to assist U.S.-Tajik dual nationals . Some areas have increased risk. Read the entire Travel Advisory..
 Terrorism 
 There are terrorist organizations in the region. There is risk of terrorist violence, including terrorist attacks and other activity in Tajikistan. Visit the U.S. Department of State’s country reports on terrorism to learn more. 
 Landmines and unexploded ordnances 
 Unexploded landmines and cluster munitions are a hazard along the Afghan-Tajik and Uzbek-Tajik borders, the Vakhsh and Rasht valleys, and in the popular hiking area of Romit. 
 Pay close attention to land mine warning signs. 
 Do not venture off the road into areas marked with red and white plastic tape for any reason. 
 Avoid roadside ditches, shoulders, and unmarked trails in these regions. 
 Never touch anything resembling unexploded munitions. 
 Some unmarked landmines may also be present in the Surobad district of GBAO and the Sarazam district. 
 U.S. government employee travel restrictions 
 U.S. government employees working in Tajikistan are not permitted to travel between cities at night. 
 U.S. government employees working in Tajikistan must obtain special authorization from the embassy security office to travel to border areas with Afghanistan due to safety risks. 
 U.S. government employees working in Tajikistan must obtain special authorization from the embassy security office to travel to GBAO due to the potential for armed conflict, in addition to receiving a special permit from the Tajik government to enter GBAO. 
 Dual nationals 
 Tajikistan does not recognize dual nationality with the United States. 
 If you are a dual U.S.-Tajik citizen or of Tajik descent, local authorities may single you out for extra questioning and harassment. 
 Dual nationals may be denied access to U.S. consular officials while in detention. 
 Reconsider travel to: 
 Tajikistan’s border with Afghanistan due to terrorism . 
 Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Oblast (GBAO) due to the potential for armed conflict .

sources.full_text:
Exercise increased caution in Tanzania due to crime, terrorism, health, unrest , arbitrary enforcement of laws , and targeting gay and lesbian individuals . Some areas have increased risk. Read the entire Travel Advisory.
 Crime 
 Violent crime happens in Tanzania. It includes assault, sexual assault, robberies, mugging, and express kidnapping.  Crime can happen at any time. It is more common in crowded urban areas and when people are not paying attention. Local law enforcement may be slow to help if a crime happens. 
 Terrorism  
 There is a risk of terrorist violence, including terrorist attacks and other activity in Tanzania. Visit the U.S. Department of State's  country reports on terrorism  to learn more. 
 Unrest 
 Demonstrations can take place in response to political or economic issues. The Tanzanian government increases security presence around protests.  This includes checkpoints and roadblocks. The Tanzanian government may limit or prohibit rallies or demonstrations.
 The government may shut down or limit internet, cell data, and phone service before, during, or after unrest. The Tanzanian government has used internet laws to punish people who share information perceived as criticizing the government.   
 Health  
 Medical services for routine and emergency procedures are limited, especially outside of the urban areas of Dar es Salaam and Arusha. Read the Health section of the Travel Guidance on this page for more information.
 Arbitrary enforcement of local laws 
 The Tanzanian government arbitrarily enforces its own laws and regulations. U.S. citizens have been detained or prevented from leaving the country for several weeks without criminal charges. The U.S. embassy cannot guarantee your release.  Local authorities do not consistently report detentions of U.S. citizens to the U.S. embassy in a timely manner. 
 Targeting of gay and lesbian individuals   
 Same-sex relationships are illegal in Tanzania and carry severe penalties.  Members of the gay and lesbian community have been arrested and harassed. Police may target people who identify as gay or lesbian.

Exercise increased caution in Zimbabwe due to crime and official harassment of U.S. citizen s.
 Opportunistic crime, such as pickpocketing, theft, and smashing of car windows with intent to steal, is common. Violent crime, such as assault, carjacking, and home invasion, also occurs. Criminals often target foreigners and residents suspected of having large sums of cash.
 Demonstrations may occur and increase in frequency around political events, such as elections. Large gatherings are often restricted by the government and can quickly escalate to violence.
 Foreigners, journalists, and non-governmental organizations may be subject to heightened scrutiny in Zimbabwe.
 Review the Travel Guidance for additional information on travel to Zimbabwe.

sources.title: Slovenia - Level 1: Exercise Normal Precautions
sources.summary: The advisory level for Slovenia remains at Level 1, indicating no increased geopolitical or security threats. The update emphasizes normal precautions with added guidance for safe hiking in the Julian Alps, reflecting routine travel safety advice rather than any elevated risk.
sources.full_text:
Exercise normal precaution in Slovenia .
 Slovenia is generally a safe destination for travelers. 
 Travelers should take standard precautions against petty crime, such as pickpocketing and purse snatching. These crimes are common in tourist areas, city centers, and transportation hubs. Use caution at night. 
 Review our Travel Guidance for Slovenia to learn how to prepare for a safe trip. 
 Exercise caution in the Julian Alps : follow local guidance, check the weather closely, dress appropriately, and never hike alone.
